title: pcdingle Picks Up Last Defender and Carries Him Toward Try Line in Tuesday's Hillhouse Fixture
subtitle: Patrick Curran's 63rd-minute run ended with a disallowed try, a yellow card, and a referee who says the handbook simply does not cover what he witnessed.
excerpt: “I’ve reffed this league for nine years. I blew the whistle because I genuinely didn’t know which law covered what I was looking at.”

bodyHTML:
Tuesday afternoon's fixture against Hillhouse School will not be remembered for the final score. It will be remembered for the 63rd minute, when Patrick Curran — known to teammates, opponents, and now apparently the entire internet as pcdingle — picked up the last defender standing between him and the try line and, by all available accounts, simply carried on running.

Witnesses on both sidelines describe the sequence the same way: Curran broke through midfield with nothing but open grass ahead of him, one Hillhouse defender got low for what should have been a routine last-ditch tackle, and Curran responded by lifting him clean off the ground and continuing toward the line with the defender still, in the words of one spectator, "tucked under his arm like a laundry basket."

"I've reffed this league for nine years. I blew the whistle because I genuinely didn't know which law covered what I was looking at. There isn't a page for this in the handbook."
— Match official, speaking after the game

The try was ultimately disallowed and Curran was shown a yellow card, though the referee reportedly spent close to two minutes conferring with both touchline coaches before settling on that as the appropriate sanction. Hillhouse's coaching staff pushed for a red; Curran's own coach argued, with what witnesses describe as visible discomfort, that "technically nobody said you can't."

The Defender Is, For The Record, Fine

The Hillhouse player involved was back on his feet immediately and finished the match, which both schools have pointed to as evidence the incident was more spectacle than danger. He declined to comment beyond a single line to a teammate, overheard pitch-side: "I had him. I definitely had him."

Curran himself was unrepentant after the final whistle, telling teammates only that he "saw a gap and took it," which several people present noted is not, strictly, what happened.
